etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowed from Latin dēvolvō (“roll or tumble off or down”), from dē- + volvō (“roll”).
senses: (intransitive) To be inherited by someone else; to pass down upon the next person in a succession, especially through failure or loss of an earlier holder. [from 16th c.]
(transitive) To delegate (a responsibility, duty, etc.) on or upon someone. [from 17th c.]
